items.label: The 3 types
items.text: Supporting (sustained contact through most of the skill) · Spotting (support at key moments only) · Shadowing (following alongside, ready to assist).

items.label: Never support
items.text: Front of neck · chest (pectorals to mid-rib) · above inner mid-thigh · buttocks/intimate areas.

items.label: Support near centre of mass
items.text: Not limb ends or joints — e.g. hips/under upper arm, not hands/wrists/knees.

items.label: Before you support
items.text: Tell the gymnast where and why: “I'll support you at the waist to help with rotation.”

items.label: Weaning off support
items.text: Padded + assisted → padded + spot/shadow → padded independent → unpadded + assisted → unpadded + spot/shadow → unpadded independent.

items.label: Accidental contact
items.text: Tell the child it was unintentional, apologise, and inform your Lead Coach, Welfare Officer and parents/carers.

items.label: Clothing
items.text: Torso fully covered, long trousers or mid-thigh-to-knee shorts. No hoodies/open pockets when supporting. No buckles or clasps.

items.label: Footwear
items.text: Socks minimum. Sliders off before supporting/demonstrating.

items.label: Hair / nails
items.text: Long hair tied back. Nails kept short for supporting.

items.label: Jewellery
items.text: All removed when providing manual support. Unremovable items (new piercings, religious/medical) must be taped/covered — tell your Manager.

items.label: Session introduction
items.text: ~2–3 min — welcome, register, readiness check, session goals.

items.label: Warm-up
items.text: ~10 min — pulse raiser → mobility → muscle activation.

items.label: Gymnastic activities
items.text: ~40–45 min — the main skill development block.

items.label: Cool-down
items.text: ~5–10 min — light cardio + self-directed stretching.

items.label: Session conclusion
items.text: <5 min — evaluate/reflect, gather feedback, positive reinforcement, finish on a high.

items.label: (based on a 60-minute session)
items.text: Scale proportionally for other durations.

items.label: Warm-up mobility
items.text: Controlled, self-directed, mobilises joints — not developing flexibility.

items.label: Warm-up muscle activation
items.text: Fundamental/gymnastics-specific patterns, prerequisites, basic shapes. Should prepare, not tire — this isn't conditioning.

items.label: Cool-down stretching
items.text: Slow, gentle, self-directed — returns muscles to resting length, not developing flexibility.

items.label: Both
items.text: Should be fun and purposeful — music, story, hand apparatus, gymnast choice.

items.label: Prerequisite
items.text: Shapes/movements/skills a gymnast must already be competent at before starting a new skill.

items.label: Technique
items.text: How the biomechanics of the movement determine what the body needs to do.

items.label: Coaching points
items.text: What the gymnast should try to do, based on technique.

items.label: Phases
items.text: The start/middle/end moments of a skill, each with its own biomechanics.

items.label: Progression
items.text: A linear sequence of activities that develop a phase or part of a skill.

items.label: Adaptation
items.text: Changing how an activity is done, or the activity itself, to suit the gymnast.

items.label: Physical preparation
items.text: Fitness-component activities (strength/balance/speed/flexibility) that support a skill — distinct from progressions.

items.label: Specificity
items.text: Relevant to the sport, skill and goal.

items.label: Progressive
items.text: Gradually increase intensity or duration.

items.label: Overload
items.text: Load must exceed what the body is used to, to adapt.

items.label: Reversibility
items.text: Fitness declines if training stops or reduces.

items.label: Tedium/variety
items.text: Vary training to prevent boredom and overuse injury.

items.label: Strength
items.text: 85–100% effort, 2–6 sets × 1–5 reps, 2–4 min rest.

items.label: Speed
items.text: 70–85% effort, 1–3 reps, short/high-intensity, 1:4 work:recovery.

items.label: Muscular endurance
items.text: 20–70% effort, 12+ reps, 3–5 sets, short rest.

items.label: Flexibility (Assistant Coach)
items.text: Self-directed methods only. Hold 15–60 sec, up to 4 times.

items.label: All 10 components
items.text: Cardiovascular endurance · Muscular endurance · Strength · Flexibility · Balance · Agility · Coordination · Power · Speed · Reaction time.

items.label: Over-challenged
items.text: <6/10 success. Low confidence, fearful. On high-risk skills this is a safety issue — adapt immediately.

items.label: Optimally challenged
items.text: ~6–8/10 success. The sweet spot for learning — still needs praise and monitoring.

items.label: Under-challenged
items.text: ~10/10 success repeatedly. Boredom — a leading cause of drop-out. Time to increase difficulty.

items.label: 1. Understand the skill
items.text: Prerequisites, technique, phases, coaching points.

items.label: 2. Progress it technically
items.text: Choose progressions and physical preparation.

items.label: 3. Progress it safely
items.text: Safe apparatus/equipment, safe manual support, individual needs, what 'success' looks like.

items.label: 4. Make it enjoyable
items.text: Organisation, coaching style, how they'll practise, which coaching skills you'll use.

items.label: Direct
items.text: ‘Show and tell’ — coach controls all information; everyone gets the same activity.

items.label: Task
items.text: ‘Set up and stand back’ — different stations for different needs; some independent practice.

items.label: Reciprocal
items.text: Paired participants give each other feedback; coach still selects content.

items.label: Guided discovery
items.text: ‘Question and involve’ — open questions lead toward a specific answer.

items.label: Problem solving
items.text: Coach sets the problem; participant finds and tests their own solution.

items.label: STEP: Space
items.text: Can everyone access the environment as set up?

items.label: STEP: Task
items.text: How will each gymnast do the activity — what would help?

items.label: STEP: Equipment
items.text: What pieces would help each gymnast succeed?

items.label: STEP: People
items.text: Who around you can offer extra support?

items.label: AIM: Open → Parallel → Modified → Specific
items.text: Same activity together → same activity, split by ability → same activity, adapted → skill practised separately before rejoining the group.

items.label: Do
items.text: Stay calm · listen without interrupting · focus only on them · tell them you must inform the Welfare Officer · reassure them it's not their fault · keep questions minimal.

items.label: Don't
items.text: Keep it to yourself · dismiss it · show shock/judgement · probe for detail · promise secrecy · decide yourself if abuse occurred · approach the accused · investigate.

items.label: Immediate danger
items.text: In the gym: tell your Lead Coach without delay (they call police). Outside the gym: call 999 yourself.

items.label: Report to
items.text: Club Welfare Officer first (or Lead Coach if unavailable). Record what was said in the child's own words, share only with the Welfare Officer.

items.label: Minimum supervision
items.text: Indirect supervision by a Lead Coach (Foundation Coach/Level 2+ or above), who must be able to observe you.

items.label: Group size
items.text: Up to 8 gymnasts under indirect supervision.

items.label: Syllabus
items.text: Only coach skills within your own syllabus, unless directly assisting a more qualified coach.

items.label: Two-adult rule
items.text: Minimum two responsible adults (18+) always present; one must be Foundation Coach qualified or above.

items.label: 1. Plan & Organise
items.text: Know your gymnasts' needs; arrive prepared and on time.

items.label: 2. Build Positive Relationships
items.text: Names, eye contact, smiling, genuine interest.

items.label: 3. Use Positive Coaching Behaviours
items.text: Role model respect and enthusiasm; praise effort; build intrinsic motivation.

items.label: 4. Effectively Communicate
items.text: Positive tone; professional language; be an EDI advocate in how you speak.

items.label: 5. Show Safe Skill Development
items.text: Prerequisites checked; logical progressions; optimal challenge.

items.label: 6. Show Technical Understanding
items.text: Technically accurate instruction, demonstration and feedback.

items.label: 7. Create & Maintain Safe & Inclusive Environments
items.text: All 5 Foundations of Duty of Care, every session.

items.label: + Evaluate & Reflect
items.text: On every session, independently and with your Lead Coach.
